implementation: Scan validated Dewy source byte spans through a retained immutable string, preserving every explicit stop guard. Reuse the existing Sloppy-derived byte-class table for identifier scanning; quoted/interpolated scanning and source slices remain checked strings.
scope: No syntax or identifier classification changes. No sentinel reads past interpolation span ends. No short-copy or allocator experiment is retained.

reference_stage.purpose: Fixed stage reference; do not replace with a slower implementation.

limits: Native 64-bit host. Warm filesystem caches; one build per binary.
C graph uses flat edges and a handwritten map; Dewy uses per-node arrays and an insertion-ordered map.
String equality uses separately allocated payloads; C uses pointer/length pairs and libc memcmp, Dewy uses runtime strings.
Kernel times exclude input generation; wall times include the complete process.
Thread CPU timing excludes descheduling, but CPU frequency and cache contention still matter.

validation.focused_coverage: Actual lexer/token/interner helpers, 20 independently expected cases, with/without excluded prefixes, interning and formatting modes, default/release. Check token kind, payload, byte span, spacing, newline and operator tags; cover truncated punctuation, base/exponent boundaries, Unicode, metatags, raw/interpolated strings and comments.

notes: Instruction counts are diagnostic, not a substitute for timed stage comparisons.
The pilot reduces large default build instructions by about 1.03%; release by 0.74%; the Jo compiler self-build is essentially unchanged.
Assembly-site counts exclude helpers; explicit stop guards remain in the hot loop.
Fresh root-line throughput and C targets remain unmet.
